kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is right that NMP drift exhibits a substantial longitudinal-vs-latitudinal asymmetry across multiple windows of the NOAA NP.xy dataset (1900–2025 yields 1.69×; 1990–2025 yields 2.16×; 2010–2025 yields 9.43×; 2020–2025 yields 2.34×) — this is a real measured feature, not a coincidence (data/wins.json:WIN-043/detail_verdict_text counter 2; verified by direct re-grep of the current 4-window parenthetical in this clone).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The asymmetry is real but the dome's specific 2.26× value is window-arbitrary — none of the four canonical windows yields 2.26× to even 5% precision (closest is 1990–2025 at 2.16×, ~4.4% off). The dome publishes no methodology specifying which window is canonical (data/wins.json:WIN-043/detail_verdict_text counter 2), so 'verifiability' (reproducing 2.16× from a public dataset) is not 'derivation' (the dome cannot say why 2.26 rather than 2.16 or 9.43). Counter (3) holds independently: the H(r) field equation depends only on radial distance, so dome geometry cannot in principle generate longitude-dependent quantities (cross-ref: §2.10 Axial Symmetry Paradox in sections.json:part2.html, where WIN-043 is explicitly cataloged among the geometrically-impossible claims).
